interpretation: Evidence verification only; sentinel synthetic intervals are not audio callbacks.

limitations: CAB wall intervals and enclosing thread-CPU intervals have different boundaries; wall minus CPU is not exclusively scheduling delay, and CPU time is not proof of DSP execution.

Sentinel intervals contain fixed arithmetic, no CAB, IR worker, automation, editor, or audio callback. Their exposure differs from CAB intervals; do not subtract sentinel elapsed times from CAB timings.
Paced means the first 1200 samples, with a 1 ms sleep after indices divisible by 8. The index-modulo-8 residue 1 is a scheduled-sleep position proxy, not measured wake-up latency.
Caller QoS observations are snapshots, not traces of priority boosts, processor migration, or host activity.
The ordinary gate is separate from all four diagnostic CAB and four sentinel populations. The 66 entries are route populations, not 66 CPU-only envelopes or a DAW/CoreAudio routing matrix.
The ordinary CTest route order is original, expanded, extended, layouts; the diagnostic probe order is original, expanded, layouts, extended. The ordinary gate is not an identical-order A/A trial.

Caller QoS also covers preparation, warmup, and sleeps and may change worker publication or fade timing. A QoS comparison measures the whole test-context intervention; retain the separate forced-publication phase.
No product performance fix, no-glitch guarantee, or relaxed acceptance policy follows from this verification.
